Member-only story Product Management Prioritization Startup How to Handle Conflicting Priorities as a Product Manager (Without Saying Yes to Everything) An improv rule, a surprising study about deadlines, and the one-hour monthly meeting that fixes your roadmap. Nova 3 min read · Nov 2, 2026 -- Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size Photo by Jeswin Thomas on Unsplash In improv, there’s one rule you learn on day one. Say “yes, and.” Whatever your scene partner offers, you accept it and build on it. Nobody blocks. The scene keeps moving. It’s also the fastest way I know to wreck a product roadmap. When you’re handling conflicting priorities as a product manager, it looks like this. Sales needs a feature to save two renewals. Customer Success has a stack of fixes. The CEO comes back from a conference with “just an idea to keep in mind.” And you say yes to all of it, because saying no feels like admitting you can’t handle the job. Three weeks later you’re apologising in every thread, and your team is working evenings on a plan that was never going to fit. If that sounds familiar, stay with me. At the end I’ll share the one change that stops people going around you straight to your engineers. It’s the part most teams skip. -- -- Written by Nova 503 followers · 35 following novatools.org Published in Nova.
